label: Paint strokes
description: Paint brush strokes on a layer in one step. On an oil or watercolour layer the medium simulates real paint; on a plain layer the brush preset draws them: pen for clean line art (pressure swells the line), pencil or charcoal to shade (light pressure, many strokes; charcoal catches the paper), marker for flat see-through tone, airbrush for soft glows, calligraphy for lettering. brush eraser (no colour) clears paint under it on its layer; remove-marks along takes whole strokes. Each stroke: points [[x,y] or [x,y,pressure]], size, colour (#rrggbb or pigment:<name>). One stroke can be many: forks grows a branch or bare tree; dabs scatters foliage, flowers or (with dab_length, angle -90) grass. Work like a painter, looking close after each passage: big shapes first; then forms in a few values (dark mass, middle, lit side); small lights and accents last.

points.description: `[[x, y], …]` or `[[x, y, pressure], …]`, pressure `0..=1`; the stroke is smoothed through them, so a few points make a curve.

brush.description: Plain layers: `pen` (crisp ink, pressure sets width), `pencil` (grainy, pressure sets darkness), `marker` (flat, overlaps darken), `airbrush` (soft spray that builds up), `charcoal` (picks up the ground's tooth), `calligraphy` (broad nib at `angle`, default 45). Any layer: `eraser` clears paint beneath it on its layer. A round ink brush when absent.

wet.description: Paint into what is still wet: blends in oil, bleeds in watercolour.
